_comment: Tier -> model per tool. Profiles in agents/ declare BOTH `model:` (a family
alias, which the harness applies natively) and `tier:` (the intent). A check in
`make verify` asserts they agree: tier-only would be silently ignored by the
harness and the subagent would run on the session default, the most expensive
tier.
NEVER write a model ID with a date suffix. Family aliases absorb version bumps
without touching thirteen files, and a guard in `make verify` enforces it.
PRICES ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT. They exist on no disk here, so a copy would be
stale the day it was written -- the defect this program pursues. The dated
record lives in docs/roadmaps/core/pipeline/021-030-program-queue.md, and
`verified_at` below makes its age visible instead of letting it rot quietly.
The `cursor` column is derived by scripts/audit_cursor_models.py (make cursor-tiers)
from the on-disk catalogue. Cursor has no subagents, so the tier applies per
PHASE (authoring vs gate) rather than per agent.
Sprint 027 human acceptance (2026-08-25): cursor.mechanical=composer-2.5,
cursor.author was grok-4.6 (effort high). cursor.gate stays null —
Design §D7 / not proven history; operational gate logs may still record Composer
as Sprint 026 did without writing the config cell (F-20260825-027).
cursor.gate remains "model": null because promotion to gate requires measured
cost per accepted unit under Cursor beyond a single sprint milestone.
Sprint 032 (2026-08-25): cursor.author promoted to grok-4.5 / high after
author-tier trial (gate rounds matched 031; Human OK at close).

gate.basis: Adversarial review and planning. Across four consecutive host sprints every central defect was found by a gate and nothing else, several after surviving their author's own verification. Cheapening the reviewer is the first thing a budget attacks and the last thing that helps.

author.basis: Structured authorship against a stated rule; downstream gates catch their errors.

mechanical.basis: Deterministic, verifiable results. A wrong answer fails at the next command.

excluded.claude-fable-5: 2x the cost of Opus ($10/$50 vs $5/$25) and requires 30-day retention, so it does not work under ZDR. It is the most capable model, which is exactly why the exclusion is written down rather than left implicit: it enters only by explicit human decision.

context_limits.haiku: 200K -- the only one of the three without 1M. The `mechanical` tier inherits this ceiling; a role in that tier handed a large context fails, and that has to be known in advance.

catalog_snapshot._purpose: The DURABLE copy, and the gate's only source. The bundled catalogue lives in a per-user temp directory the system clears and CI never has, so a gate reading it directly would silently never fire there -- a mechanism wired where it cannot run (RA-16). This snapshot is committed, so `--check` works everywhere; refreshing it from the bundled file is the opportunistic half.
